questions.prompt: State the type of wave made by ripples on a water surface.
questions.answer: Transverse.

questions.prompt: State the type of wave that sound travels through air as.
questions.answer: Longitudinal.

questions.prompt: State what longitudinal waves consist of.
questions.answer: Areas of compression and rarefaction.

questions.prompt: Define a transverse wave.
questions.answer: A wave in which the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer (the direction the wave travels).

questions.prompt: Define a longitudinal wave.
questions.answer: A wave in which the oscillations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer (the direction the wave travels).

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between longitudinal and transverse waves.
questions.answer: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer; in a longitudinal wave they are parallel to it (and form compressions and rarefactions).

questions.prompt: Define a compression in a longitudinal wave.
questions.answer: A region where the particles are squashed close together.

questions.prompt: Define a rarefaction in a longitudinal wave.
questions.answer: A region where the particles are spread further apart.

questions.prompt: Describe evidence that, for ripples on a water surface, it is the wave and not the water that travels.
questions.answer: A floating object (e.g. a cork) just bobs up and down on the spot as the ripples pass; it is not carried along with the wave.

questions.prompt: Define the amplitude of a wave.
questions.answer: The maximum displacement of a point on the wave from its undisturbed position.

questions.prompt: Define the wavelength of a wave.
questions.answer: The distance from a point on one wave to the equivalent point on the adjacent wave.

questions.prompt: Define the frequency of a wave.
questions.answer: The number of waves passing a point each second (measured in hertz, Hz).

questions.prompt: Define the period of a wave.
questions.answer: The time taken for one complete wave to pass a point (T = 1 ÷ f).

questions.prompt: Define wave speed.
questions.answer: The speed at which energy is transferred (or the wave moves) through the medium.

questions.prompt: Calculate the speed of a wave with a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 0.4 m.
State the unit of wavelength.
questions.answer: Metres (m).

questions.prompt: State the unit of period.
questions.answer: Seconds (s).

questions.prompt: Calculate the period of a wave with a frequency of 50 Hz.
State the three things that can happen to a wave at the boundary between two materials.
questions.answer: It can be reflected, transmitted or absorbed.

questions.prompt: Define 'transmitted' for a wave at a boundary.
questions.answer: The wave passes through the boundary into the second material.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the energy of a wave that is absorbed by a material.
questions.answer: It is transferred to the internal (thermal) energy store of the material.

questions.prompt: Define 'reflected' for a wave at a boundary.
questions.answer: The wave bounces back off the boundary.

questions.prompt: State the range of frequencies that normal human hearing covers.
questions.answer: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.prompt: Define ultrasound.
questions.answer: Sound waves with a frequency above the upper limit of human hearing (above 20 kHz).

questions.prompt: Name the part of the ear that vibrates when sound waves reach it.
questions.answer: The ear drum.

questions.prompt: State whether P-waves are transverse or longitudinal.
questions.answer: Longitudinal.

questions.prompt: State whether S-waves can travel through a liquid.
questions.answer: No.

questions.prompt: State how ultrasound is used to find the distance to a boundary.
questions.answer: The time taken for reflections to return to a detector is measured and used to calculate the distance.

questions.prompt: Define seismic waves.
questions.answer: Waves produced by earthquakes.

questions.prompt: State whether S-waves are transverse or longitudinal.
questions.answer: Transverse.

questions.prompt: State what P-waves and S-waves provide evidence for.
questions.answer: The structure and size of the Earth’s core.

questions.prompt: State what echo sounding is used for.
questions.answer: Detecting objects in deep water and measuring water depth, using high frequency sound waves.

questions.prompt: Name the group of electromagnetic waves with the longest wavelength.
questions.answer: Radio waves.

questions.prompt: Name the group of electromagnetic waves with the highest frequency.
questions.answer: Gamma rays.

questions.prompt: State whether all types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same speed through a vacuum.
questions.answer: Yes.

questions.prompt: Define electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer: Transverse waves that transfer energy from the source of the waves to an absorber.

questions.prompt: State the seven groups of the electromagnetic spectrum in order, from longest to shortest wavelength.
questions.answer: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

questions.prompt: State which part of the electromagnetic spectrum the human eye can detect.
questions.answer: Visible light only.

questions.prompt: Define refraction.
questions.answer: The change in direction of a wave as it crosses the boundary between two media at an angle, caused by the change in speed of the wave.

questions.prompt: State what causes refraction.
questions.answer: The difference in velocity of the waves in different substances.

questions.prompt: State four things that can happen to an electromagnetic wave at a boundary between two substances.
questions.answer: It can be absorbed, transmitted, refracted or reflected (in ways that vary with wavelength).

questions.prompt: State the type of electromagnetic wave used in fibre optic communications.
questions.answer: Visible light.

questions.prompt: State the type of electromagnetic wave used in satellite communications.
questions.answer: Microwaves.

questions.prompt: State the types of electromagnetic wave used in medical imaging and treatment.
questions.answer: X-rays and gamma rays.

questions.prompt: State a use of radio waves.
questions.answer: Television and radio.

questions.prompt: State a use of infrared waves.
questions.answer: Electrical heaters, cooking food or infrared cameras (any one).

questions.prompt: State a use of ultraviolet waves.
questions.answer: Energy efficient lamps or sun tanning (either one).

questions.prompt: State which electromagnetic wave can cause skin to age prematurely and increases the risk of skin cancer.
questions.answer: Ultraviolet.

questions.prompt: State which electromagnetic waves are ionising and can cause mutation of genes and cancer.
questions.answer: X-rays and gamma rays.

questions.prompt: State the type of electromagnetic wave produced by oscillations in electrical circuits.
questions.answer: Radio waves.

questions.prompt: State where gamma rays originate.
questions.answer: From changes in the nucleus of an atom.

questions.prompt: Define the focal length of a lens.
questions.answer: The distance from the lens to the principal focus.

questions.prompt: State whether the image produced by a concave lens is real or virtual.
questions.answer: Always virtual.

questions.prompt: Define the principal focus of a convex lens.
questions.answer: The point where parallel rays of light are brought to a focus by the lens.

questions.prompt: Define magnification.
questions.answer: Image height ÷ object height (a ratio, so it has no units).

questions.prompt: State how a lens forms an image.
questions.answer: By refracting light.

title: Reflection and colour of visible light

questions.prompt: Define specular reflection.
questions.answer: Reflection from a smooth surface in a single direction.

questions.prompt: Define diffuse reflection.
questions.answer: Reflection from a rough surface, which scatters light in many directions.

questions.prompt: State the colour of an opaque object that absorbs all wavelengths of visible light.
questions.answer: Black.

questions.prompt: State what determines the colour of an opaque object.
questions.answer: Which wavelengths of light are more strongly reflected (the wavelengths that are not reflected are absorbed).

questions.prompt: State how a colour filter works.
questions.answer: It absorbs certain wavelengths (colours) and transmits other wavelengths (colours).

questions.prompt: State the two types of object that transmit light.
questions.answer: Transparent and translucent objects.

questions.prompt: State whether all bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation.
questions.answer: Yes, at any temperature.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the amount of infrared radiation emitted by a hotter body.
questions.answer: A hotter body emits more infrared radiation in a given time.

questions.prompt: Define a perfect black body.
questions.answer: An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it.

questions.prompt: State why a perfect black body is the best possible emitter of radiation.
questions.answer: A good absorber is also a good emitter, and a perfect black body absorbs all radiation incident on it.
